issues.title: [Epic · Post-MVP Product] Player inspiration, discovery, practice, and return loop
issues.outcome: Evaluate and deliver a small local-first player companion that turns trusted wiki information into explainable inspiration, play decisions, deliberate improvement, and healthy reasons to return to Arcaea.
scope: Define the player problem and the choose → play → optional reflection → adapt loop.
Coordinate player research, explainable discovery/practice support, local-first progress, and confidence-aware community knowledge.
Preserve the wiki as the public factual foundation and independent fallback.
Set explicit entry criteria, success measures, non-goals, scope cuts, and rollback.
nonGoals: Do not change or delay Web MVP 0.1.
Do not begin with accounts, social feeds, global leaderboards, cloud sync, a recommendation backend, or hosted personal data.
Do not use punitive streaks, shame, forced urgency, fabricated scarcity, or black-box ranking.
Do not scrape player accounts, official services, protected charts, or third-party wiki databases.
acceptanceCriteria: Web MVP 0.1 has passed the public-preview gate before implementation begins.
Research identifies a concrete player problem beyond lookup and catalog discovery.
The selected vertical slice is explainable, optional, local-first where personal data exists, and sustainable for one maintainer.
Legal, privacy, deletion, accessibility, security, moderation, and maintenance boundaries are approved.
The public wiki remains fully usable with the companion disabled or unavailable.
Success can be evaluated without invasive tracking.
definitionOfDone: Relevant product decisions, documentation, tests, and rollback are updated.
No unreviewed legal, accessibility, security, privacy, performance, moderation, or maintenance exception is introduced.

issues.title: [Post-MVP Product] Validate player inspiration, choice, improvement, and return problems
issues.outcome: Identify which post-MVP player problem is valuable enough to solve before building a companion feature.
scope: Interview or diary-study beginner, returning, progressing, and experienced players.
Study how players choose songs, plan short sessions, respond to difficulty walls, use wikis, and return after breaks.
Validate willingness to enter optional local data and the minimum useful feedback.
Compare no-feature, editorial discovery, deterministic guidance, and personalized local-first approaches.
Select one narrow vertical slice or explicitly decide not to build.
nonGoals: Do not recruit only high-Potential or highly engaged players.
Do not present modeled personas or maintainer intuition as completed research.
Do not collect credentials, replay files, private profiles, or unnecessary personal data.
Do not implement recommendation or progression code in this issue.
acceptanceCriteria: Research questions, participant segments, consent, data minimization, and analysis method are documented.
Evidence distinguishes lookup needs from inspiration, decision, practice, reflection, and return needs.
The report includes alternatives, failure cases, device/ownership constraints, and reasons players reject suggestions.
A selected problem has measurable user value, a legal data path, and a sustainable smallest slice.
Weak evidence results in retaining the wiki without companion expansion.
definitionOfDone: Research evidence and the go/no-go decision are reviewable.
No unnecessary personal data is retained.

issues.title: [Post-MVP Product] Explainable discovery, short sessions, and practice ladders
issues.outcome: Help a player choose a useful next song or short session with transparent reasoning grounded in reviewed catalog data and clearly labeled observations.
scope: Define validated intents such as discover, warm up, practice a skill, push difficulty, recover after a break, or play casually.
Create deterministic rules for daily discovery, short-session composition, alternatives, and ownership/unlock constraints.
Model skill tags, chart-demand profiles, bridge-song relationships, and practice ladders with method, provenance, confidence, and version applicability.
Explain why each suggestion was produced and what information is uncertain.
Use legal official outbound listening/source links instead of hosting protected media.
nonGoals: Do not claim objective difficulty or player suitability from unsupported proxies.
Do not use a black-box model, engagement-maximizing ranker, leaderboard, or paywall optimization.
Do not require chart files, audio, replay data, accounts, or a backend for the first slice.
Do not fabricate suggestions for songs lacking sufficient reviewed data.
acceptanceCriteria: Every suggestion exposes inputs, rationale, limits, confidence, and an alternative.
Subjective/community signals remain distinct from verified facts.
The same supported inputs produce deterministic results for the initial rules-based slice.
Users can reject or replace a suggestion without penalty.
Missing ownership, unlock, version, platform, or skill data degrades gracefully.
The feature can be disabled without affecting wiki routes.
definitionOfDone: Acceptance criteria are verified with representative fixtures and player walkthroughs.
Explanations, limitations, accessibility, and rollback are documented.
No post-MVP service becomes a wiki dependency.

issues.title: [Post-MVP Product] Local-first goals, reflection, progress, export, and recovery
issues.outcome: Let players optionally record lightweight goals and reflections that improve future guidance without creating an account or uploading personal play data.
scope: Define the minimum local profile and reflection fields justified by research.
Support inspect, edit, export, import, reset, delete, schema migration, and storage-failure recovery.
Use low-friction feedback only when validated, such as too easy, good fit, too hard, retry later, fatigue, or a private note.
Make privacy status and local-only behavior visible.
Design supportive comeback behavior after a break.
nonGoals: Do not require exact scores, Potential, replay uploads, credentials, or cloud synchronization.
Do not use punitive streaks, loss framing, shame, forced notifications, or dark patterns.
Do not infer health, skill, or identity attributes from sparse local data.
Do not retain data after explicit deletion.
acceptanceCriteria: No personal progress data leaves the device by default.
Users can inspect, export, import, and delete all stored data.
Malformed imports, quota failures, interrupted writes, and migrations preserve the last valid dataset.
The wiki remains usable when storage is unavailable or persistence is declined.
Breaks and missed sessions do not remove earned state or trigger punitive messaging.
Any sync requires a separate security, privacy, cost, and operations decision.
definitionOfDone: Acceptance criteria are verified across storage and recovery failures.
Privacy, data lifecycle, accessibility, migration, and rollback are documented.
All personal data can be removed without affecting the wiki catalog.

issues.title: [Post-MVP Community] Confidence-aware difficulty, latency, Potential, and player research
issues.outcome: Evaluate whether community observations can add useful player knowledge without presenting subjective, biased, private, or stale conclusions as verified fact.
scope: Evaluate subjective difficulty dimensions, device latency reports, Potential research, skill tags, and practice relationships.
Require method, sample context, population/device/version scope, confidence, dissent, review status, and correction history.
Define contribution, moderation, dispute, abuse, privacy, retention, and removal workflows.
Compare repository-reviewed submissions with voting, comments, forms, and hosted community systems.
Pilot only one bounded research workflow after maintainer approval.
nonGoals: Do not publish one universal difficulty tier as objective truth.
Do not collect account identifiers, private play history, or unnecessary device fingerprints.
Do not open unmoderated comments, polls, or uploads without sustainable ownership.
Do not let community observations overwrite verified catalog facts.
acceptanceCriteria: Every published observation identifies method, context, confidence, scope, review date, and correction path.
Verified facts and community observations remain separate in schema and UI.
Moderation and dispute workload is measured against solo-maintainer capacity.
Low-sample, stale, conflicting, or biased results remain visibly limited or unpublished.
Participants understand what data is public, retained, corrected, and removed.
The pilot can be stopped and removed without damaging the core catalog.
definitionOfDone: Acceptance criteria are verified through a bounded pilot or a documented no-go decision.
Governance, privacy, moderation, confidence, correction, and removal behavior are documented.
Community conclusions never become verified facts without independent evidence.
